text:
Dear student,
This book contains all the information you need to
know to get acquainted with exchange opportunities
at NU. Please refer to the table of contents below for
guidance. 
At the moment of publishing this material (October
31, 2025), all the processes in regard to mobility
programs were factual and based on the then-
current partner universities. 
As of the latest update (February 7, 2026), the
application process, eligibility to participate,
information on the current SSH School Manager, as
well as several minor procedural details have been
updated.
Please note that over time, new changes and
partnerships can be implemented, while those
mentioned here may no longer be accurate. 
Best wishes,
Ministry of Education
1
Preface

text:
Benefits of Academic Mobility 
Eligibility to Participate 
Experience living abroad and adapting to a new
environment
Develop responsibility, maturity, and independence
Improve English proficiency through daily practice
Strengthen communication and interpersonal skills
Gain a deeper understanding of different traditions,
cultures, and lifestyles
Build lasting friendships and global connections
Access high-quality education at the host university
*Undergraduate students must complete at least 2 semesters, while
graduate students must complete at least 1 semester. Keep in mind that for
Undergraduates, 1st and 4th year students are not eligible for exchange.
3
Full-time NU students who are at least 18 years old* 
Applicants must be on good academic standing (CGPA
3.00 or above out of 4.00; no misconduct cases)
Applicants must show an aptitude, motivation, and
maturity to thrive in the environment of the host
country
No incomplete grades in any courses and no
disciplinary violations
Insight: Based on the experience of exchange students it is
essential to have a high academic standing and engagement
in extracurricular activities (particularly leadership positions)

text:
Forms of Academic Mobility
4
Academic Exchange 
One or two semesters credit bearing program on a
reciprocal basis with subsequent transfer of credits. Inter-
institutional agreement (IIA) is a must. 
Note: Exchange students are nominated by Home
Institutions (NU Schools).
Study Abroad / Module Programs 
Study modules that are credit bearing program at Host
Institution on a non-reciprocal basis, with the possibility of
transfer of credits. 
Research Internships 
These programs allow students to undertake research
experiences preliminary approved by School (credit
bearing / non-credit bearing).
Cultural Mobility 
Short-term cultural exploration visit abroad (1 week to 1
month, non-credit bearing).

text:
Application Submission 
Applicant must submit to the School Selection Committee
the following documents:
Application form 
Resume or CV
Statement of purpose*
Official transcript of academic record 
Official enrollment verification form 
Recommendation letter from a faculty member or
advisor
While the aforementioned documents are the standard
application package, each School or Academic Program
may require additional documents. It is the responsibility
of students to consider specific requirements.
*There are no specific requirements for the statement of purpose. It should
be written by the applicant and indicate the reasons why the School
Selection Committee should choose you among the other applicants. Please
specify your expectations from participating in this program, your motivation
and future plans 
6

text:
Important Points Before and
After Completion
When nominated for the exchange, ensure that the courses
you plan to take at the Host Institution are discussed with
your School’s Academic Manager, approved by the
Department Chair or Program Director, and have NU
equivalents in order to be officially transferred later.
After completing an Academic Exchange or Study Abroad
program, the Host Institution must send a physical copy of
the official transcript to the Department of
Internationalization (DI), which will forward it to the School
for credit transfer.
Course grades from these programs are not included in
the NU CGPA, except in cases of “Fail” or its equivalent. In
other words, the system of credit transfer works by the
Pass/Fail. The Registrar’s Office does not inform the School
of student grades, as the School is already aware.
Upon their return, NU outgoing exchange students must
start attending classes at NU within the first week of the
new semester.
Students are responsible for coordinating with their
professors to catch up on any missed coursework. NU does
not guarantee that absences due to mobility will be
excused.
7

text:
DI or CAC? 
Students often tend to confuse these two structures
because, at first glance, they seem the same as they are
closely working with students and providing them with
various opportunities. Here is an overview:
The Department of Internationalization (DI) promotes
and coordinates student mobility programs, and is mainly
responsible for the following:
Calling for applications 
Sending documents of selected students to the Host
Institutions 
Approval of exchange programs proposed from outside
by students
Career Advising Center (CAC) assists NU students with
internships, job search, interview skills, resume review,
alumni issues, and graduate application, hence:
Educating in experiential learning programs
Connecting students and alumni with internships
provided by the employers 
Facilitate Internship programs in cooperation with NU
schools 
8

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What are the possible expenses to expect?
A: Although programs may provide financial aid and cover
the expenses, normally students are expected to pay for:
2-way flight tickets
Accommodation
Visa 
Medical Insurance
Food 
Miscellaneous 
Q: Does NU have Erasmus+ agreements?
A: Yes, NU has numerous agreements for Student Mobility
programs within the framework of the Erasmus program.
Q: Can students find and participate in mobility
programs on their own?
A: Yes, NU students can participate in Student Mobility
programs on their own. However, the respective NU School
still has to approve the program as credit-bearing. 
Q: Who announces mobility opportunities?
A: Each School announces exchange opportunities via
email with all the requirements and set deadlines. 
Q: How long do student mobility programs usually last?
A: The most common period of academic exchange for
most students is one semester. However, the duration of
student mobility programs can vary, ranging from a few
weeks to a full academic year.
12

text:
Q: Are mobility programs free for NU students?
A: Mobility opportunities provided by NU based on NU
cooperation links usually include Tuition fee waiver. Other
expenses (2-way air fare, accommodation, food
expenses/costs, visa fee, medical insurance, miscellaneous
expenses and additional university fees) are covered by the
student. 
Q: What are possible challenges along the student
mobility program?
A: Challenges can include cultural adjustment, language
barriers, homesickness, differences in educational systems,
administrative complexities related to visa and travel
regulations, and financial differences for living expenses.
Q: Can I participate in academic mobility if I have a
family or dependents?
A: There are no restrictions for students with families or
dependents. However, visa issues and all the costs for
their expenses should be borne by students.
Q: Do I need to know the local language to participate in
an academic mobility program?
A: Many courses at Host Institutions are usually offered in
English, while some of them might require proficiency in
the local language. Always check the language
requirements of the specific program/course you're
interested in.
Frequently Asked Questions
